Update a model's elements and the frames they are declared at

Source: R/update-model.R
update-model-method.Rd

Writes @geoframe / @timeframe on the named elements and on every object pinned to them, and the slots given in data. It changes no value: a declaration that does not already sit at the requested frame is refused, naming the object and the column.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'model'
update(
  object,
  geoframe = NULL,
  timeframe = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  force = FALSE,
  dryrun = FALSE,
  verbose = isVerbose(),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a model.

geoframe

named frame requests, list(ELC = "zone") or c(ELC = "zone"); the element is a commodity, technology or storage.

timeframe

the same on the time axis, for a commodity, technology or weather.

data

named list of per-object slot updates, list(DEM_ELC = list(demand = dem_zone)), each handed to that object's own update().

force

write the frames although data is not at them, with a warning naming what is left inconsistent – the sequential route. The model will not interpolate until the data follows.

dryrun

return the report instead of the model, changing nothing.

verbose

report what moved.

...

unused.

Value

The updated model, or the report when dryrun = TRUE.

Details

A commodity's frame is where it balances, and the strict classes carrying it – demand, supply, import, export, trade, storage – are pinned to it, so they move with it or the call refuses. Those flows have no aggregation path, which is why they cannot sit at a frame of their own.

data is applied BEFORE the frames move, so a single call carrying both the re-keyed data and the new frame has nothing left to refuse. Moving data is otherwise a separate operation, and upward only – see aggregate_model_regions() – because the balance layer only aggregates.

See also

Other model: find_in_model(), get_region(), get_weather()

Examples

# \donttest{
kit <- topia$modules$electricity
mod <- newModel("TOPIA", data = kit$repo,
                calendar = topia$modules$calendars$d365_h24,
                region = kit$regions,
                horizon = topia$modules$horizons$BY2025_50_by10,
                discount = 0.05)
mod <- setGeoscale(mod, kit$geoscale)

# what moving ELC to the zone would ask for
update(mod, geoframe = list(ELC = "zone"), dryrun = TRUE)
#> ELC: geoframe province -> zone (17 objects)
#> 
#> Data is not at the requested frame:
#>   STG_ELC          storage    capacity$region                R11, R12
#>   TBD_ELC_R02_R03  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R02, R03
#>   TBD_ELC_R02_R05  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R02, R05
#>   TBD_ELC_R04_R05  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R04, R05
#>   TBD_ELC_R04_R06  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R04, R06
#>   TBD_ELC_R05_R06  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R05, R06
#>   TBD_ELC_R02_R07  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R02, R07
#>   TBD_ELC_R03_R07  trade      invcost$region, routes$dst, routes$src, ... (7) R03, R07
#>   ... and 8 more object(s): DEM_ELC, TBD_ELC_R05_R07, TBD_ELC_R06_R10, TBD_ELC_R07_R08, TBD_ELC_R08_R09, TBD_ELC_R09_R10, ... (8) 
#> 
#> Endpoints (src/dst) are a network decision, not a recast: one route per child or one shared route.
#> 
#> Move the data first -- aggregate_model_regions(), or declare it at the frame -- then update the frame. force = TRUE writes the frame now and leaves the data to a later call.
# }
